issues.current: Operating unlicensed carries a civil penalty of up to $3,000 and enforcement action.
issues.correct: Unlicensed operation is subject to the penalties of the Nursing Home Care Act (210 ILCS 9/25). The general Act penalty is up to $5,000 per violation, and each day counts as a separate violation (Sec. 135(a)). The $3,000 cap applies only to keeping a resident who exceeds the care needs defined in the Act (Sec. 135(b)).
issues.evidence: Sec. 25: "An entity that operates as an assisted living or shared housing establishment ... without a license shall be subject to the provisions, including penalties, of the Nursing Home Care Act." P.A. 104-0589 text of Sec. 135: "civil penalty not to exceed $5,000 ... Each day a violation continues shall be deemed a separate violation."
issues.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'Operating unlicensed makes the entity subject to the Nursing Home Care Act penalties (210 ILCS 9/25). Separately, the Act allows civil penalties up to $5,000 per violation per day (210 ILCS 9/135).' Remove the $3,000 figure.

issues.current: Confirm current manager training-hour requirements with IDPH. A 2012 proposed-amendment text mentions 20 hours every two years, but it is outdated and not verified against the current code.
issues.correct: The statute itself requires the director to complete at least 20 hours of training every 2 years as a condition of licensure (210 ILCS 9/35). It is a current legal requirement, not an outdated proposal.
issues.evidence: Sec. 35 (as reprinted in P.A. 104-0589): "as a condition of licensure under this Act, the director of an establishment must participate in at least 20 hours of training every 2 years".
issues.fix: State the requirement as: 'Director must complete at least 20 hours of training every 2 years (210 ILCS 9/35, a condition of licensure).' Budget the courses explicitly. Also update opex 'Training...' notes, which say the manager training-hour requirement was not verified.

issues.current: Pre-admission comprehensive assessment 'may be completed by' a physician, PA or APRN. The RN/LPN lines are labelled 'assessments' (for example, al20_private: 'RN/LPN ... assessments, service plans').
issues.correct: The text says the comprehensive assessment 'shall be completed by' a physician, a physician assistant or an APRN. It is mandatory and restrictive, not permissive. An RN/LPN cannot be the one who completes the pre-admission, annual or change-of-condition comprehensive assessment. For dementia programs, annual and change-of-condition assessments must be signed by a physician. The model has no cost line for these physician/PA/APRN assessments, which is a missing mandatory cost.
issues.evidence: Sec. 15: "a comprehensive assessment ... shall be completed by a physician, a physician assistant, or an advanced practice registered nurse." Sec. 150(c): annual or change-of-condition assessments "must be signed by a physician."
issues.fix: Reword 'may be completed by' to 'must be completed by'. Remove 'assessments' from the RN/LPN role descriptions, or state that the RN supports but does not complete the assessment. Add a per-admission and annual line for physician/PA/APRN comprehensive assessments (cost unverified, so get quotes). Confirm the 2026-07-24 effective date: the fetched text did not show it, and Sec. 15 cites an earlier P.A. 104-191 effective 1-1-26.

issues.current: Benefits are a flat 6% operator estimate. No line exists for mandatory paid leave or a state retirement program.
issues.correct: Illinois requires paid leave under the Paid Leave for All Workers Act (about 1 hour per 40 worked, up to 40 hours a year). Chicago employers also have the Chicago Paid Leave and Paid Sick and Safe Leave Ordinance. Employers with 5 or more employees and no retirement plan may owe Illinois Secure Choice enrollment. This comes from general knowledge and was not fetched.
issues.fix: Confirm the figures on labor.illinois.gov and the Chicago Office of Labor Standards. Show mandatory paid leave and any Secure Choice obligation as explicit items. Check whether 6% covers paid leave on about 4+ FTE aides plus premium-pay coverage for absences.
